1198	// handleSessionPostChanges is the session-scoped batch commit over the same
1199	// change collection the session reads page:
1200	//
1201	//	POST /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes
1202	//
1203	// The request body carries only the changes array — the calling device is the
1204	// session's owning device, resolved with the same identity rule as the
1205	// session reads, exports and subscriptions; no new credential is introduced
1206	// and no device id travels in the body. Per-element semantics and the success
1207	// body are byte-identical to the document-level commit: results arrive in
1208	// request order, each naming its id, whether it was created and the cursor it
1209	// was assigned. The checks run in the fixed order request shape (400),
1210	// session existence (404), document permission (403) — the permission verdict
1211	// is taken inside the commit transaction, so a revoked device writes nothing —
1212	// and a payload/device mismatch against an existing id is a 409 reporting the
1213	// conflicting id. Every rejection leaves the log untouched.
1214	func handleSessionPostChanges(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1215		sessionID := r.PathValue("sessionId")   // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1216		documentID := r.PathValue("documentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1217	
1218		var req sessionPostRequest
1219		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
1220			return
1221		}
1222		if len(req.Changes) == 0 {
1223			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "changes must be a non-empty array")
1224			return
1225		}
1226	
1227		changes := make([]events.Change, len(req.Changes))
1228		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(req.Changes))
1229		for i, c := range req.Changes {
1230			if c.ID == "" {
1231				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each change must have a non-empty string id")
1232				return
1233			}
1234			if len(c.Payload) == 0 {
1235				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each change must carry a JSON payload")
1236				return
1237			}
1238			if _, dup := seen[c.ID]; dup {
1239				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "duplicate change id within batch: "+c.ID)
1240				return
1241			}
1242			seen[c.ID] = struct{}{}
1243			changes[i] = events.Change{ID: c.ID, Payload: c.Payload}
1244		}
1245	
1246		// Request shape is settled; only now does the session lookup run, so a
1247		// malformed batch against an unknown session is still a 400.
1248		deviceID, err := s.SessionDevice(sessionID)
1249		if err != nil {
1250			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSessionNotFound) {
1251				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
1252				return
1253			}
1254			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up session")
1255			return
1256		}
1257		for i := range changes {
1258			changes[i].DeviceID = deviceID
1259		}
1260	
1261		results, err := s.PostSessionChanges(documentID, changes)
1262		if err != nil {
1263			var conflict *events.ErrConflict
1264			switch {
1265			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
1266				// The session's device was deregistered between the lookup and
1267				// the commit; its cascade removed the session too, so the
1268				// identity the caller used no longer exists.
1269				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
1270			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrPermissionDenied):
1271				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
1272			case errors.As(err, &conflict):
1273				writeJSON(w, http.StatusConflict, map[string]string{
1274					"error":      "change id already exists with different deviceId or payload",
1275					"conflictId": conflict.ID,
1276				})
1277			default:
1278				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to commit changes")
1279			}
1280			return
1281		}
1282	
1283		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"results": results})
1284	}

1569			// at the transport): nothing more to write and nothing was stored.
1570			return
1571		case err != nil:
1572			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to poll changes")
1573			return
1574		}
1575	
1576		writePollPage(w, changes, nextCursor, timedOut)
1577	}
1578	
1579	// handleReplay retries an offline batch against the existing change log. The
1580	// request and per-element semantics mirror POST .../changes — strict
1581	// application/json body, non-empty ids, no in-batch duplicates, idempotent only
1582	// when deviceId and decoded payload match, otherwise 409 reporting the
1583	// conflicting id — with the registration/permission layer enforced first:
1584	// 404 for an unregistered device and 403 for a revoked one, neither exposing
1585	// change content. The whole batch commits in one serialized transaction that
1586	// shares the document's contiguous cursor space with ordinary commits.
1587	func handleReplay(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1588		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1589	
1590		var req replayRequest
1591		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
1592			return
1593		}
1594		if req.DeviceID == "" {
1595			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "deviceId must be a non-empty string")
1596			return
1597		}
1598		if req.Operations == nil {
1599			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "operations must be a non-empty array")
1600			return
1601		}
1602		if len(req.Operations) == 0 {
1603			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "operations must be a non-empty array")
1604			return
1605		}
1606	
1607		changes := make([]events.Change, len(req.Operations))
1608		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(req.Operations))
1609		for i, op := range req.Operations {
1610			if op.ID == "" {
1611				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each operation must have a non-empty string id")
1612				return
1613			}
1614			if len(op.Payload) == 0 {
1615				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each operation must carry a JSON payload")
1616				return
1617			}
1618			if _, dup := seen[op.ID]; dup {
1619				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "duplicate operation id within batch: "+op.ID)
1620				return
1621			}
1622			seen[op.ID] = struct{}{}
1623			changes[i] = events.Change{ID: op.ID, DeviceID: req.DeviceID, Payload: op.Payload}
1624		}
1625	
1626		results, err := s.ReplayChanges(documentID, changes)
1627		if err != nil {
1628			var conflict *events.ErrConflict
1629			switch {
1630			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
1631				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "device not found")
1632			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrPermissionDenied):
1633				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
1634			case errors.As(err, &conflict):
1635				writeJSON(w, http.StatusConflict, map[string]string{
1636					"error":      "operation id already exists with different deviceId or payload",
1637					"conflictId": conflict.ID,
1638				})
1639			default:
1640				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to replay operations")
1641			}
1642			return
1643		}
1644	
1645		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"results": results})
1646	}

1	// Package app is the composition root: it opens the one shared database and
2	// constructs the three independently reusable internal services — the change
3	// event service, the permission service and the CRDT state service — wiring
4	// them together only through their internal interfaces.
5	//
6	// The services share one SQLite connection (the kernel opens a single
7	// pooled connection with immediate transactions), so a change commit, a CRDT
8	// submission or compaction, and a permission change are serialized on the
9	// same connection and leave no half-written batch. The change event and CRDT
10	// services take their registration-and-authorization verdict from the
11	// permission service inside their own transactions (events.Gate / crdt.Gate),
12	// and the permission service fans a committed revoke out to their
13	// subscription registries through authz.RevokeSink. No service reaches into
14	// another service's tables or fields.
15	//
16	// App is the single object the entry and HTTP layers use. It promotes each
17	// service's input/output boundary as its methods while hiding the wiring; it
18	// adds no authentication and exposes no endpoint of its own.
19	package app
20	
21	import (
22		"context"
23		"encoding/json"
24		"time"
25	
26		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/authz"
27		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/crdt"
28		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/events"
29		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
30	)
31	
32	// App composes the durable kernel and the three internal services over one
33	// shared database connection.
34	type App struct {
35		*store.Store
36	
37		events *events.Service
38		crdt   *crdt.Service
39	
40		// Authz is the permission service. It is exposed so the HTTP layer can
41		// grant/revoke and read authorization directly; the other services reach
42		// it through their gates rather than this field.
43		Authz *authz.Service
44	}
45	
46	// Open opens (creating if needed) the SQLite database at path and constructs
47	// every internal service over it. The empty path opens a private in-memory
48	// database useful for tests. A construction failure closes the kernel and
49	// leaves nothing behind.
50	func Open(path string) (*App, error) {
51		kernel, err := store.Open(path)
52		if err != nil {
53			return nil, err
54		}
55	
56		// The permission service is built first: its gate is a constructor
57		// dependency of the change event and CRDT services.
58		permissions, err := authz.New(kernel)
59		if err != nil {
60			_ = kernel.Close()
61			return nil, err
62		}
63		eventService, err := events.New(kernel, permissions)
64		if err != nil {
65			_ = kernel.Close()
66			return nil, err
67		}
68		crdtService, err := crdt.New(kernel, permissions)
69		if err != nil {
70			_ = kernel.Close()
71			return nil, err
72		}
73	
74		// A committed revoke ends the affected live subscriptions in both
75		// push channels. The dependency is an interface, registered once here, so
76		// the permission service never names either subscriber concretely.
77		permissions.AddRevokeSink(eventsRevokeSink{eventService})
78		permissions.AddRevokeSink(crdtService)
79	
80		return &App{
81			Store:  kernel,
82			events: eventService,
83			crdt:   crdtService,
84			Authz:  permissions,
85		}, nil
86	}
87	
88	// eventsRevokeSink adapts the change event service's revoke hook to the
89	// permission service's RevokeSink interface.
90	type eventsRevokeSink struct{ e *events.Service }
91	
92	func (s eventsRevokeSink) PermissionRevoked(documentID, deviceID string) {
93		s.e.SignalRevoked(documentID, deviceID)
94	}
95	
96	// Events returns the change event service.
97	func (a *App) Events() *events.Service { return a.events }
98	
99	// CRDT returns the CRDT state service.
100	func (a *App) CRDT() *crdt.Service { return a.crdt }
101	
102	// ---- Change event service boundary (promoted so the entry layer has one
103	// object; each method delegates verbatim to the events service). ----
104	
105	// InterruptWaits wakes every parked long poll and every live change-log and
106	// CRDT subscription without closing the database, so an orderly shutdown
107	// drains waiting connections (long polls answer 503; subscriptions finish
108	// with the going-away close) instead of holding the drain hostage.
109	func (a *App) InterruptWaits() {
110		a.events.InterruptWaits()
111		a.crdt.InterruptWaits()
112	}
113	
114	// Closing reports whether shutdown has begun, covering both push channels.
115	func (a *App) Closing() bool {
116		return a.events.Closing() || a.crdt.Closing()
117	}
118	
119	// Close interrupts the in-memory observers, waits for every subscription
120	// handler to unregister and then releases the shared database handle.
121	func (a *App) Close() error {
122		a.events.InterruptWaits()
123		a.crdt.InterruptWaits()
124		a.events.WaitDrained()
125		a.crdt.WaitDrained()
126		return a.Store.Close()
127	}
128	
129	// PostChanges delegates to the change event service.
130	func (a *App) PostChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
131		return a.events.PostChanges(documentID, changes)
132	}
133	
134	// ReplayChanges delegates to the change event service.
135	func (a *App) ReplayChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
136		return a.events.ReplayChanges(documentID, changes)
137	}
138	
139	// PostSessionChanges commits a batch whose device identity was resolved from
140	// a session by the HTTP layer, delegating to the change event service's
141	// gated commit: the registration/permission verdict is taken inside the same
142	// serialized transaction as the write, so a revoked device commits nothing.
143	func (a *App) PostSessionChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
144		return a.events.CommitAuthorized(documentID, changes)
145	}
146	
147	// ReplaySessionChanges replays an offline batch whose device identity was
148	// resolved from a session by the HTTP layer; it is the session counterpart
149	// to ReplayChanges and commits through the same gated transaction the
150	// session-scoped batch commit uses, so the two paths cannot drift.
151	func (a *App) ReplaySessionChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
152		return a.events.CommitAuthorized(documentID, changes)
153	}
154	
155	// MergeChange delegates to the change event service.
156	func (a *App) MergeChange(documentID string, baseCursor int64, c events.Change) (events.MergeResult, error) {
157		return a.events.MergeChange(documentID, baseCursor, c)
158	}
159	
160	// PutSnapshot delegates to the change event service.
161	func (a *App) PutSnapshot(documentID string, cursor int64, state json.RawMessage) (bool, error) {
162		return a.events.PutSnapshot(documentID, cursor, state)
163	}
164	
165	// GetSnapshot delegates to the change event service.
166	func (a *App) GetSnapshot(documentID string, cursor int64) (json.RawMessage, error) {
167		return a.events.GetSnapshot(documentID, cursor)
168	}
169	
170	// ExportSnapshots delegates to the change event service. A nil to means the
171	// interval has no upper bound.
172	func (a *App) ExportSnapshots(documentID string, from int64, to *int64) ([]events.ExportedSnapshot, error) {
173		return a.events.ExportSnapshots(documentID, from, to)
174	}
175	
176	// RestoreSnapshot delegates to the change event service.
177	func (a *App) RestoreSnapshot(documentID, deviceID, changeID string, snapshotCursor int64) (events.RestoreResult, error) {
178		return a.events.RestoreSnapshot(documentID, deviceID, changeID, snapshotCursor)
179	}
180	
181	// ListChanges delegates to the change event service.
182	func (a *App) ListChanges(documentID string, after, limit int64) ([]events.ListedChange, int64, error) {
183		return a.events.ListChanges(documentID, after, limit)
184	}
185	
186	// ExportChanges delegates to the change event service. A nil to means the
187	// interval has no upper bound.
188	func (a *App) ExportChanges(documentID string, from int64, to *int64) ([]events.ListedChange, error) {
189		return a.events.ExportChanges(documentID, from, to)
190	}
191	
192	// WaitForChanges delegates to the change event service.
193	func (a *App) WaitForChanges(ctx context.Context, documentID string, after, limit int64, wait time.Duration) ([]events.ListedChange, int64, bool, error) {
194		return a.events.WaitForChanges(ctx, documentID, after, limit, wait)
195	}
196	
197	// DocumentExists delegates to the change event service.
198	func (a *App) DocumentExists(documentID string) (bool, error) {
199		return a.events.DocumentExists(documentID)
200	}
201	
202	// CompactChanges delegates to the change event service.
203	func (a *App) CompactChanges(documentID, deviceID string) (boundary, removed int64, err error) {
204		return a.events.CompactChanges(documentID, deviceID)
205	}
206	
207	// AddSubscription delegates to the change event service.
208	func (a *App) AddSubscription(documentID, deviceID string) (<-chan struct{}, <-chan struct{}, func()) {
209		return a.events.AddSubscription(documentID, deviceID)
210	}
211	
212	// DeregisterDevice removes a registered device together with every record it
213	// owns — its sessions, the attachments it created (chunks, sealed state and
214	// unfinished uploads included), the access grants it held, and its
215	// document-permission rows — all in one serialized transaction that commits
216	// synchronously. An unknown or already deregistered device yields
217	// store.ErrDeviceNotFound and writes nothing, so a repeat deregistration
218	// misses exactly the way a never-registered id does and concurrent calls take
219	// effect at most once. Shared digest-addressed content is reclaimed only when
220	// the last completed attachment referencing it is gone; other devices'
221	// changes, snapshots and document content are untouched.
222	//
223	// After the commit the same id may register again as a brand-new device — no
224	// session, permission or attachment is inherited — and every live
225	// subscription the device held across both push channels is ended
226	// immediately, stickily.
227	func (a *App) DeregisterDevice(deviceID string) error {
228		tx, err := a.Store.DB().Begin()
229		if err != nil {
230			return err
231		}
232		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
233	
234		if err := store.DeleteDeviceTx(tx, deviceID); err != nil {
235			return err
236		}
237		if err := a.Authz.DeleteDevicePermissionsTx(tx, deviceID); err != nil {
238			return err
239		}
240		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
241			return err
242		}
243	
244		// End the device's live subscriptions only after the cascade is durable:
245		// a reconnect attempt after the close finds the backing session gone
246		// (404), so the connection cannot immediately re-establish itself.
247		a.events.SignalDeviceDeregistered(deviceID)
248		a.crdt.SignalDeviceDeregistered(deviceID)
249		return nil
250	}
251	
252	// ---- Permission service boundary. ----
253	
254	// SetDocumentPermission delegates to the permission service.
255	func (a *App) SetDocumentPermission(documentID, deviceID string, authorized bool) (bool, error) {
256		return a.Authz.SetDocumentPermission(documentID, deviceID, authorized)
257	}
258	
259	// DocumentAuthorized delegates to the permission service.
260	func (a *App) DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID string) (bool, error) {
261		return a.Authz.DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID)
262	}
263	
264	// ListDocumentPermissions delegates to the permission service.
265	func (a *App) ListDocumentPermissions(documentID string, limit, offset int64) ([]authz.PermissionEntry, error) {
266		return a.Authz.ListDocumentPermissions(documentID, limit, offset)
267	}
268	
269	// ---- CRDT state service boundary. ----
270	
271	// SubmitCRDTOps delegates to the CRDT state service.
272	func (a *App) SubmitCRDTOps(documentID, declaredType string, ops []crdt.Op) ([]crdt.Result, error) {
273		return a.crdt.SubmitOps(documentID, declaredType, ops)
274	}
275	
276	// GetCRDTState delegates to the CRDT state service.
277	func (a *App) GetCRDTState(documentID string) (crdt.State, error) {
278		return a.crdt.GetState(documentID)
279	}

282	func (a *App) CompactCRDT(documentID, deviceID string) (crdt.Snapshot, error) {
283		return a.crdt.Compact(documentID, deviceID)
284	}

286	// GetCRDTSnapshot delegates to the CRDT state service.
287	func (a *App) GetCRDTSnapshot(documentID string) (crdt.Snapshot, error) {
288		return a.crdt.GetSnapshot(documentID)
289	}
290	
291	// OpenCRDTSubscription delegates to the CRDT state service.
292	func (a *App) OpenCRDTSubscription(documentID, deviceID string) (*crdt.State, *crdt.Subscription, func(), error) {
293		return a.crdt.OpenSubscription(documentID, deviceID)
294	}

297	func (a *App) AddCRDTSubscription(documentID, deviceID string) (*crdt.Subscription, func()) {

1	// Package events is the change event service: the durable per-document change
2	// log together with everything written on top of it.
3	//
4	// Within a document every change has a client-supplied id. New ids receive a
5	// monotonically increasing cursor; re-posting an existing id is idempotent
6	// only when the deviceId and decoded JSON payload match, otherwise it is a
7	// conflict. Valid batches commit atomically in one serialized transaction, so
8	// cursors never repeat and no record is partially written, even under
9	// concurrent writers. Ordinary posts, offline replays, merges and snapshot
10	// restores all allocate from the same per-document contiguous cursor space.
11	//
12	// A document may also carry snapshots: caller-supplied JSON states pinned to
13	// existing change cursors. Snapshots are write-once per cursor — a matching
14	// re-post is idempotent, a differing one a conflict — and live apart from the
15	// change log. A restore appends an ordinary change whose payload is a
16	// snapshot's state, recording its provenance so a repeated restore after a
17	// restart keeps the same idempotency/conflict decisions.
18	//
19	// Reads page by cursor in ascending order. The session view and the document
20	// view are the same read; the HTTP layer adds the session/permission checks.
21	// Long polling and push subscriptions are in-memory observers of commits:
22	// they register before the confirming read, hold no durable state, and are
23	// woken only after a change-bearing transaction has committed.
24	//
25	// The service owns only its own tables. The registration and permission
26	// layers are reached through its Gate interface, so a replay or merge never
27	// reaches into another service's storage.
28	package events
29	
30	import (
31		"encoding/json"
32		"errors"
33		"fmt"
34	)
35	
36	// ErrStoreClosing reports that the service is shutting down and parked long
37	// polls have been woken so they can return without writing anything. The
38	// caller maps it to 503.
39	var ErrStoreClosing = errors.New("store is closing")
40	
41	// Change is one element of an inbound batch or one row of a listing.
42	type Change struct {
43		ID       string          // client-supplied change id, unique per document
44		DeviceID string          // originating device
45		Payload  json.RawMessage // decoded JSON value, stored verbatim
46	}
47	
48	// Result reports the outcome for one element of an accepted batch.
49	type Result struct {
50		ID      string `json:"id"`
51		Created bool   `json:"created"`
52		Cursor  int64  `json:"cursor"`
53	}
54	
55	// ListedChange is one row in a ListChanges response.
56	type ListedChange struct {
57		ID       string          `json:"id"`
58		DeviceID string          `json:"deviceId"`
59		Payload  json.RawMessage `json:"payload"`
60		Cursor   int64           `json:"cursor"`
61	}
62	
63	// MergeResult reports the outcome of an accepted MergeChange. Outcome is one
64	// of "idempotent", "applied" or "merged".
65	type MergeResult struct {
66		ID      string  `json:"id"`
67		Outcome string  `json:"outcome"`
68		Cursor  int64   `json:"cursor"`
69		Result  *Result `json:"result,omitempty"`
70	}
71	
72	// ErrConflict reports that a batch references an existing change id with a
73	// different deviceId or payload. The whole batch is rejected.
74	type ErrConflict struct {
75		ID string
76	}
77	
78	func (e *ErrConflict) Error() string {
79		return fmt.Sprintf("conflicting change %q for document", e.ID)
80	}
81	
82	// ErrStaleCursor reports that a merge targets a base cursor for an unknown
83	// document, or a base cursor greater than the document's current cursor. The
84	// caller maps it to 400; nothing is written.
85	var ErrStaleCursor = errors.New("baseCursor is unknown or ahead of the current cursor")
86	
87	// ErrSnapshotBase reports that a snapshot targets an unknown document or a
88	// cursor that is not an existing change cursor of the document. The caller
89	// maps it to 400; nothing is written.
90	var ErrSnapshotBase = errors.New("snapshot cursor is not an existing cursor of the document")
91	
92	// ErrCompactedBase reports that a merge targets a base cursor below the
93	// document's compaction boundary: the changes it would be checked against
94	// have left the online log, so the conflict check cannot be completed. The
95	// caller maps it to 400; nothing is written.
96	var ErrCompactedBase = errors.New("baseCursor is below the compaction boundary")
97	
98	// ErrSnapshotNotFound reports that no snapshot exists for the document and
99	// cursor. The caller maps it to 404.
100	var ErrSnapshotNotFound = errors.New("snapshot not found")
101	
102	// ErrSnapshotConflict reports that a snapshot already exists for the document
103	// and cursor with a different state. The stored snapshot is left unchanged.
104	type ErrSnapshotConflict struct {
105		Cursor int64
106	}
107	
108	func (e *ErrSnapshotConflict) Error() string {
109		return fmt.Sprintf("conflicting snapshot for cursor %d", e.Cursor)
110	}
111	
112	// ErrRestoreConflict reports that a restore references a change id that is
113	// already taken by an ordinary change, or by a prior restore whose deviceId,
114	// snapshot cursor or source state differs. Nothing is written; the caller maps
115	// it to 409.
116	type ErrRestoreConflict struct {
117		ID string
118	}
119	
120	func (e *ErrRestoreConflict) Error() string {
121		return fmt.Sprintf("change id %q conflicts with the change log", e.ID)
122	}
123	
124	// ExportedSnapshot is one row of an ExportSnapshots result.
125	type ExportedSnapshot struct {
126		Cursor int64           `json:"cursor"`
127		State  json.RawMessage `json:"state"`
128	}
129	
130	// RestoreResult reports the outcome of an accepted RestoreSnapshot.
131	type RestoreResult struct {
132		ID           string `json:"id"`
133		Created      bool   `json:"created"`
134		Cursor       int64  `json:"cursor"`
135		RestoredFrom int64  `json:"restoredFrom"`
136	}
137	
138	// schema is created when the service is constructed. Table and index shapes
139	// are unchanged from the pre-refactor layout, so data already on disk stays
140	// readable.
141	const schema = `
142	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS changes (
143		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
144		cursor      INTEGER NOT NULL,
145		id          TEXT NOT NULL,
146		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
147		payload     BLOB NOT NULL,
148		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, id)
149	);
150	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS changes_doc_cursor_idx
151		ON changes(document_id, cursor);
152	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS snapshots (
153		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
154		cursor      INTEGER NOT NULL,
155		state       BLOB NOT NULL,
156		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, cursor)
157	);
158	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS restores (
159		document_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
160		change_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
161		device_id       TEXT NOT NULL,

1	// Package store is the durable kernel shared by the internal services: it
2	// owns the SQLite database handle and the registration layer (devices and
3	// sessions) plus resumable attachments.
4	//
5	// The business services layered on top of the kernel — the change event log,
6	// the permission ledger and the CRDT state — live in their own packages and
7	// cooperate only through their internal interfaces. They all share this one
8	// handle: it opens a single pooled connection with immediate write
9	// transactions, so every service's transactional judgment is serialized on
10	// the same connection and no batch is ever half written.
11	//
12	// Devices and sessions form the registration layer. A device registers with a
13	// client-supplied id; a session belongs to exactly one registered device and
14	// is addressed by its own client-supplied id. Registration and session
15	// creation are idempotent re-posts: the first call creates, an identical
16	// repeat does not. A session id already owned by another device is a
17	// conflict, never silently re-homed. Deletes are owner-scoped and hard: a
18	// repeat delete, another device, and a cross-device path all miss with 404,
19	// after which the id is free to be created again. A device itself can
20	// deregister: the device row and everything it owns — its sessions and the
21	// attachments it created, chunks and grants included — vanish in one
22	// serialized transaction, a repeat or never-registered deregistration misses
23	// with 404 and writes nothing, and the freed id registers again as a
24	// brand-new device.
25	//
26	// Attachments are resumable chunked uploads owned by the registered device
27	// that created them. Creation pins the declared total size, chunk size and
28	// SHA-256 digest; chunks land in any order and are stored durably as they
29	// arrive, so an interrupted upload resumes after a restart with its
30	// idempotency and conflict decisions intact. Finishing concatenates the
31	// chunks, verifies the digest and seals the upload; a sealed upload is
32	// immutable and rejects every further chunk write. Finished content is
33	// addressed by digest, so a second attachment with the same digest and size
34	// reuses the stored bytes instead of copying them. The creator may grant
35	// other registered devices read-only access per attachment; every
36	// (attachment, device) pair starts unauthorized, grants and revokes commit in
37	// the same serialized way, and access never widens the write paths. Deletes
38	// are owner-scoped and hard: the record, its chunks and its grants vanish in
39	// one serialized transaction, a repeat delete misses with 404, the id is free
40	// to be created again, and the shared content bytes are reclaimed once the
41	// last completed attachment referencing them is gone.
42	package store
43	
44	import (
45		"database/sql"
46		"encoding/json"
47		"errors"
48		"fmt"
49	
50		_ "modernc.org/sqlite"
51	)

53	// ErrDeviceNotFound reports that an operation targets a device id that was
54	// never registered. Services map it to 404; nothing is written.
55	var ErrDeviceNotFound = errors.New("device not found")

58	// revoked. Services map it to 403; nothing is written and no document content
59	// is exposed. It is a shared verdict produced by the permission service and
60	// consulted by every service that enforces the gate inside a transaction.
61	var ErrPermissionDenied = errors.New("device permission for this document has been revoked")

67		ID string

79	// DBTX is the subset of *sql.DB and *sql.Tx the services use for their
80	// serialized work, so judgments made "in the same transaction" (for example a
81	// permission gate followed by the gated write) run on one concrete connection
82	// whether the caller holds a transaction or the handle itself.
83	type DBTX interface {
84		Exec(query string, args ...any) (sql.Result, error)
85		Query(query string, args ...any) (*sql.Rows, error)
86		QueryRow(query string, args ...any) *sql.Row
87	}

89	// Store is the durable kernel: one SQLite database handle together with the
90	// device, session and attachment data it owns.
91	type Store struct {
92		db *sql.DB
93	}
94	
95	// Open opens (creating if needed) the SQLite database at path. The empty path
96	// opens an in-memory database useful for tests.
97	func Open(path string) (*Store, error) {
98		if path == "" {
99			// With a single pooled connection this is a private, per-instance
100			// in-memory database (useful for tests).
101			path = "file::memory:"
102		}
103		// _txlock=immediate makes writers acquire the write lock at BEGIN, so
104		// concurrent batches serialize without SQLITE_BUSY deadlocks.
105		dsn := path + "?_txlock=immediate&_busy_timeout=5000&_journal_mode=WAL&_synchronous=FULL&_foreign_keys=on"
106		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", dsn)
107		if err != nil {
108			return nil, err
109		}
110		// One connection avoids cross-connection locking surprises; writes are
111		// serialized by the immediate transaction anyway, and SQLite concurrency
112		// for readers does not help correctness here. It also keeps every
113		// service's transaction serialized on the same connection.
114		db.SetMaxOpenConns(1)
115		s := &Store{db: db}
116		if err := s.init(); err != nil {
117			_ = db.Close()
118			return nil, err
119		}
120		return s, nil
121	}
122	
123	// DB returns the underlying handle. The business services use it to open the
124	// serialized transactions their judgments run in; callers outside the
125	// internal packages never need it.
126	func (s *Store) DB() *sql.DB { return s.db }
127	
128	// Close releases the database handle.
129	func (s *Store) Close() error {
130		return s.db.Close()
131	}

153	);

155		attachment_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES attachments(id),
156		idx           INTEGER NOT NULL,
157		data          BLOB NOT NULL,
158		PRIMARY KEY (attachment_id, idx)
159	);

173		if err != nil {
174			return err

182	// ensureAttachmentCreatedSeq adds the creation-order column to databases
183	// created before it existed. Existing rows are backfilled in insertion
184	// (rowid) order so their relative listing order is unchanged; new rows take
185	// strictly larger values, so the sequence never reuses a value even after
186	// the newest attachment is deleted and its id created again.
187	func (s *Store) ensureAttachmentCreatedSeq() error {
188		rows, err := s.db.Query(`PRAGMA table_info(attachments)`)
189		if err != nil {
190			return err
191		}
192		hasColumn := false
193		for rows.Next() {
194			var cid, notNull, pk int
195			var name, colType string
196			var dflt sql.NullString
197			if err := rows.Scan(&cid, &name, &colType, &notNull, &dflt, &pk); err != nil {
198				_ = rows.Close()
199				return err
200			}
201			if name == "created_seq" {
202				hasColumn = true
203			}
204		}
205		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
206			_ = rows.Close()
207			return err
208		}
209		_ = rows.Close()
210		if hasColumn {
211			return nil
212		}
213		if _, err := s.db.Exec(
214			`ALTER TABLE attachments ADD COLUMN created_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`,
215		); err != nil {
216			return err
217		}
218		_, err = s.db.Exec(
219			`UPDATE attachments SET created_seq = (
220				SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attachments older WHERE older.rowid <= attachments.rowid
221			)`,
222		)
223		return err
224	}

226	// ensureAttachmentAccessGrantedSeq adds the grant-order column to access
227	// tables created before it existed. Existing rows are backfilled one past the
228	// per-attachment maximum in insertion (rowid) order, so surviving grants keep
229	// a stable relative order; every new grant takes a strictly larger value, even
230	// after the previously newest grant was revoked, so a re-granted device lists
231	// at the position of its latest grant and a value is never reused.
232	func (s *Store) ensureAttachmentAccessGrantedSeq() error {
233		rows, err := s.db.Query(`PRAGMA table_info(attachment_access)`)
234		if err != nil {
235			return err
236		}
237		hasColumn := false
238		for rows.Next() {
239			var cid, notNull, pk int
240			var name, colType string
241			var dflt sql.NullString
242			if err := rows.Scan(&cid, &name, &colType, &notNull, &dflt, &pk); err != nil {
243				_ = rows.Close()
244				return err
245			}
246			if name == "granted_seq" {
247				hasColumn = true
248			}
249		}
250		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
251			_ = rows.Close()
252			return err
253		}
254		_ = rows.Close()
255		if hasColumn {
256			return nil
257		}
258		if _, err := s.db.Exec(
259			`ALTER TABLE attachment_access ADD COLUMN granted_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`,
260		); err != nil {
261			return err
262		}
263		_, err = s.db.Exec(
264			`UPDATE attachment_access SET granted_seq = (
265				SELECT rn FROM (
266					SELECT rowid AS rid,
267					       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY attachment_id ORDER BY rowid) AS rn
268					FROM attachment_access
269				) WHERE rid = attachment_access.rowid
270			)`,
271		)
272		return err
273	}

275	// RegisterDevice registers a device by client-supplied id. The first call for
276	// an id creates it and reports created=true; repeating the registration is
277	// idempotent (created=false). Device identity never changes.
278	func (s *Store) RegisterDevice(deviceID string) (created bool, err error) {
279		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
280		if err != nil {
281			return false, err
282		}
283		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
284	
285		created, err = RegisterDeviceTx(tx, deviceID)
286		if err != nil {
287			return false, err
288		}
289		return created, tx.Commit()
290	}
291	
292	// RegisterDeviceTx is RegisterDevice against an existing transaction, so the
293	// services can resolve the registration layer as the first step of a larger
294	// serialized transaction (their permission/content gates then share it).
295	func RegisterDeviceTx(q DBTX, deviceID string) (created bool, err error) {
296		var exists bool
297		if err := q.QueryRow(
298			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
299		).Scan(&exists); err != nil {
300			return false, err
301		}
302		if !exists {
303			if _, err := q.Exec(`INSERT INTO devices (id) VALUES (?)`, deviceID); err != nil {
304				return false, err
305			}
306			return true, nil
307		}
308		return false, nil
309	}

311	// DeviceExistsTx reports whether deviceID is registered, evaluated inside q so
312	// a service's gate runs on the same transaction as the work it guards.
313	func DeviceExistsTx(q DBTX, deviceID string) (bool, error) {
314		var exists bool
315		if err := q.QueryRow(
316			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
317		).Scan(&exists); err != nil {
318			return false, err
319		}
320		return exists, nil
321	}

323	// CreateSession creates a session owned by deviceID with a client-supplied id.
324	//
325	//   - An unknown device yields ErrDeviceNotFound; nothing is written.
326	//   - A session id already owned by another device yields *ErrSessionConflict;
327	//     nothing is written and the owner is unchanged.
328	//   - Re-posting the same (device, session) pair is idempotent: created=false.
329	//
330	// A deleted session is gone for good, so its id can be registered again as a
331	// brand-new session (created=true). The lookup, owner check and insert run in
332	// one serialized transaction, so concurrent creates of the same session id
333	// cannot both create it.
334	func (s *Store) CreateSession(deviceID, sessionID string) (created bool, err error) {
335		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
336		if err != nil {
337			return false, err
338		}
339		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
340	
341		var deviceExists bool
342		if err := tx.QueryRow(
343			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
344		).Scan(&deviceExists); err != nil {
345			return false, err
346		}
347		if !deviceExists {
348			return false, ErrDeviceNotFound
349		}
350	
351		var owner string
352		err = tx.QueryRow(
353			`SELECT device_id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?`, sessionID,
354		).Scan(&owner)
355		switch {
356		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
357			if _, err := tx.Exec(
358				`INSERT INTO sessions (id, device_id) VALUES (?, ?)`,
359				sessionID, deviceID,
360			); err != nil {
361				return false, err
362			}
363			if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
364				return false, err
365			}
366			return true, nil
367		case err != nil:
368			return false, err
369		}
370	
371		if owner != deviceID {
372			return false, &ErrSessionConflict{ID: sessionID}
373		}
374		return false, tx.Commit()
375	}

377	// DeleteSession removes the live session matching the (deviceID, sessionID)
378	// pair. Any miss — the session does not exist, was already deleted, or belongs
379	// to another device — returns ErrSessionNotFound and changes nothing. The
380	// check and the delete run in one transaction, so a concurrent create cannot
381	// interleave and a repeat delete still misses; the removal is committed to
382	// disk before the call returns.
383	func (s *Store) DeleteSession(deviceID, sessionID string) error {
384		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
385		if err != nil {
386			return err
387		}
388		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
389	
390		var owner string
391		err = tx.QueryRow(
392			`SELECT device_id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?`, sessionID,
393		).Scan(&owner)
394		switch {
395		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
396			return ErrSessionNotFound
397		case err != nil:
398			return err
399		}
400		if owner != deviceID {
401			return ErrSessionNotFound
402		}
403	
404		if _, err := tx.Exec(
405			`DELETE FROM sessions WHERE id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
406			sessionID, deviceID,
407		); err != nil {
408			return err
409		}
410		return tx.Commit()
411	}
412	
413	// DeleteDeviceTx deregisters deviceID and removes every record it owns, all
414	// inside the caller's serialized transaction:
415	//
416	//   - the device's sessions are hard-deleted, so their session-scoped reads
417	//     and subscriptions miss from then on;
418	//   - every attachment it created is removed together with its chunks, its
419	//     sealed/unfinished state and the access rows other devices held on it;
420	//   - the read grants the device itself held on other devices' attachments
421	//     are withdrawn;
422	//   - the device row is removed last (every child row goes first).
423	//
424	// Digest-addressed content is shared across attachments and is reclaimed only
425	// when no completed attachment still references a digest — exactly the rule
426	// of a single attachment delete — so another device's attachment with the same
427	// digest keeps its bytes and one deregistration by itself never reclaims
428	// shared content. The document permission ledger lives in the authz package
429	// and clears its own rows against the same transaction through
430	// DeleteDevicePermissionsTx.
431	//
432	// An unknown (never registered or already deregistered) device yields
433	// ErrDeviceNotFound and writes nothing. Because the whole judgment runs in one
434	// immediate transaction on the single shared connection, concurrent
435	// deregistrations of the same device commit at most once and any concurrent
436	// chunk upload or finish either committed entirely before it or is rejected
437	// entirely afterward — no half-written record survives.
438	func DeleteDeviceTx(q DBTX, deviceID string) error {
439		exists, err := DeviceExistsTx(q, deviceID)
440		if err != nil {
441			return err
442		}
443		if !exists {
444			return ErrDeviceNotFound
445		}
446	
447		// Remember the digests of the device's completed attachments before their
448		// rows vanish: each is a candidate for content reclamation once every
449		// owned attachment is gone. DISTINCT because several of the device's
450		// attachments may share the same digest-addressed content.
451		rows, err := q.Query(
452			`SELECT DISTINCT sha256 FROM attachments WHERE device_id = ? AND complete = 1`,
453			deviceID,
454		)
455		if err != nil {
456			return err
457		}
458		var digests []string
459		for rows.Next() {
460			var digest string
461			if err := rows.Scan(&digest); err != nil {
462				_ = rows.Close()
463				return err
464			}
465			digests = append(digests, digest)
466		}
467		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
468			_ = rows.Close()
469			return err
470		}
471		if err := rows.Close(); err != nil {
472			return err
473		}
474	
475		// Withdraw the read grants this device held on other devices'
476		// attachments (rows naming it as the grantee), then remove the access
477		// rosters of the attachments it created before the attachment rows those
478		// rosters reference are deleted.
479		if _, err := q.Exec(
480			`DELETE FROM attachment_access WHERE device_id = ?`, deviceID,
481		); err != nil {
482			return err
483		}
484		if _, err := q.Exec(
485			`DELETE FROM attachment_access
486			 WHERE attachment_id IN (SELECT id FROM attachments WHERE device_id = ?)`,
487			deviceID,
488		); err != nil {
489			return err
490		}
491		if _, err := q.Exec(
492			`DELETE FROM attachment_chunks
493			 WHERE attachment_id IN (SELECT id FROM attachments WHERE device_id = ?)`,
494			deviceID,
495		); err != nil {
496			return err
497		}
498		if _, err := q.Exec(
499			`DELETE FROM attachments WHERE device_id = ?`, deviceID,
500		); err != nil {
501			return err
502		}
503	
504		// Reclaim each digest-addressed content only when no surviving completed
505		// attachment — owned by another device, or by the deregistered device in
506		// an impossible re-read — still references it.
507		for _, digest := range digests {
508			var stillReferenced bool
509			if err := q.QueryRow(
510				`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM attachments WHERE sha256 = ? AND complete = 1)`,
511				digest,
512			).Scan(&stillReferenced); err != nil {
513				return err
514			}
515			if !stillReferenced {
516				if _, err := q.Exec(
517					`DELETE FROM attachment_contents WHERE sha256 = ?`, digest,
518				); err != nil {
519					return err
520				}
521			}
522		}
523	
524		if _, err := q.Exec(
525			`DELETE FROM sessions WHERE device_id = ?`, deviceID,
526		); err != nil {
527			return err
528		}
529		if _, err := q.Exec(
530			`DELETE FROM devices WHERE id = ?`, deviceID,
531		); err != nil {
532			return err
533		}
534		return nil
535	}

539	// require that the session currently exists.
540	func (s *Store) SessionExists(sessionID string) (bool, error) {
541		var exists bool
542		if err := s.db.QueryRow(
543			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM sessions WHERE id = ?)`, sessionID,
544		).Scan(&exists); err != nil {
545			return false, err
546		}
547		return exists, nil

550	// SessionDevice returns the id of the device that owns the live session
551	// sessionID. A session that was never created or was deleted yields
552	// ErrSessionNotFound.
553	func (s *Store) SessionDevice(sessionID string) (string, error) {
554		var deviceID string
555		err := s.db.QueryRow(
556			`SELECT device_id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?`, sessionID,
557		).Scan(&deviceID)
558		switch {
559		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
560			return "", ErrSessionNotFound
561		case err != nil:
562			return "", err
563		default:
564			return deviceID, nil
565		}

568	// JSONEqual reports whether two payloads are equal after JSON decoding, so
569	// 1 and 1.0, or {"a":1,"b":2} and {"b":2,"a":1}, compare equal. It is shared
570	// verbatim by the change event and CRDT services' idempotency judgments.
571	func JSONEqual(a, b json.RawMessage) bool {
572		var va, vb any
573		if err := json.Unmarshal(a, &va); err != nil {
574			return false
575		}
576		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &vb); err != nil {
577			return false
578		}
579		return deepEqual(va, vb)
580	}
581	
582	func deepEqual(a, b any) bool {
583		switch av := a.(type) {
584		case nil:
585			return b == nil
586		case bool:
587			bv, ok := b.(bool)
588			return ok && av == bv
589		case string:
590			bv, ok := b.(string)
591			return ok && av == bv
592		case float64:
593			bv, ok := b.(float64)
594			return ok && av == bv
595		case []any:
596			bv, ok := b.([]any)
597			if !ok || len(av) != len(bv) {
598				return false
599			}
600			for i := range av {
601				if !deepEqual(av[i], bv[i]) {
602					return false
603				}
604			}
605			return true
606		case map[string]any:
607			bv, ok := b.(map[string]any)
608			if !ok || len(av) != len(bv) {
609				return false
610			}
611			for k, v := range av {
612				w, exists := bv[k]
613				if !exists || !deepEqual(v, w) {
614					return false
615				}
616			}
617			return true
618		default:
619			return false
620		}

1	// Package authz is the permission service: the durable, per-document and
2	// per-device authorization ledger together with the system's single revoke
3	// verdict.
4	//
5	// Every (document, device) pair starts authorized; a grant or revoke is
6	// recorded per pair. The lookup and the write run in one serialized
7	// transaction on the shared connection and commit to disk, so concurrent
8	// grant/revoke calls each land as a complete state and survive a restart.
9	//
10	// The other services do not read the permission table. They take their
11	// registration-and-authorization verdict through AuthorizedTx, evaluated
12	// inside their own write transaction, so a rejected request is judged before
13	// any document content is observed and the gate and the gated work commit as
14	// one judgment. Revoking never deletes changes, snapshots, sessions or CRDT
15	// state; it only produces the denial and, after the revoke commits, notifies
16	// the registered revoke sinks (the live subscription registries) so they can
17	// end the affected connections with the one-time, sticky 4403 close.
18	package authz
19	
20	import (
21		"database/sql"
22		"errors"
23		"sync"
24	
25		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
26	)
27	
28	// schema is created when the service is constructed; its shape is unchanged
29	// from the pre-refactor layout, so authorization rows already on disk stay
30	// readable.
31	const schema = `
32	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS document_permissions (
33		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
34		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
35		authorized  INTEGER NOT NULL,
36		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, device_id)
37	);
38	`
39	
40	// RevokeSink observes a committed revoke. The change event service and the
41	// CRDT service register themselves to end the affected live subscriptions; a
42	// sink must not block and must be safe to call after the revoke transaction
43	// has committed. The permission service depends on this interface alone, so
44	// the dependency points from the observers toward the verdict and never back.
45	type RevokeSink interface {
46		PermissionRevoked(documentID, deviceID string)
47	}
48	
49	// Service is the permission service.
50	type Service struct {
51		db *sql.DB
52	
53		mu    sync.Mutex
54		sinks []RevokeSink
55	}
56	
57	// New constructs the permission service over the shared kernel handle and
58	// creates its table.
59	func New(kernel *store.Store) (*Service, error) {
60		db := kernel.DB()
61		if _, err := db.Exec(schema); err != nil {
62			return nil, err
63		}
64		return &Service{db: db}, nil
65	}
66	
67	// AddRevokeSink registers an observer notified after every committed revoke.
68	// It is called by the composition root while wiring the services, before the
69	// surface serves requests.
70	func (s *Service) AddRevokeSink(sink RevokeSink) {
71		s.mu.Lock()
72		s.sinks = append(s.sinks, sink)
73		s.mu.Unlock()
74	}
75	
76	// AuthorizedTx is the shared gate: it returns nil when deviceID is registered
77	// and currently authorized for documentID, store.ErrDeviceNotFound when the
78	// device is not registered and store.ErrPermissionDenied when its access has
79	// been revoked. It runs inside the caller's transaction q, so the verdict is
80	// taken on the same serialized connection as the work it guards, before any
81	// document content is read.
82	func (s *Service) AuthorizedTx(q store.DBTX, documentID, deviceID string) error {
83		exists, err := store.DeviceExistsTx(q, deviceID)
84		if err != nil {
85			return err
86		}
87		if !exists {
88			return store.ErrDeviceNotFound
89		}
90		var stored int
91		err = q.QueryRow(
92			`SELECT authorized FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
93			documentID, deviceID,
94		).Scan(&stored)
95		switch {
96		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
97			// No deviation row: devices start authorized.
98			return nil
99		case err != nil:
100			return err
101		default:
102			if stored == 0 {
103				return store.ErrPermissionDenied
104			}
105			return nil
106		}
107	}
108	
109	// DeviceAuthorizedTx adapts the shared gate to the change event and CRDT
110	// services' Gate interface (which names *sql.Tx). The verdict is identical.
111	func (s *Service) DeviceAuthorizedTx(tx *sql.Tx, documentID, deviceID string) error {
112		return s.AuthorizedTx(tx, documentID, deviceID)
113	}
114	
115	// SetDocumentPermission grants or revokes deviceID's access to documentID and
116	// reports whether the stored permission actually changed.
117	//
118	// Every device starts authorized for every document, so the first revoke is
119	// the first write for the pair (changed=true); repeating a state that already
120	// holds writes nothing and reports changed=false. An unregistered device
121	// yields store.ErrDeviceNotFound and nothing is written. The lookup and the
122	// write run in one serialized transaction, so concurrent grant/revoke calls
123	// each commit completely and the final state matches the last committed
124	// action. After a revoke commits, every registered sink is notified; a grant
125	// notifies nothing (a prior revoke already ended the connection stickily).
126	func (s *Service) SetDocumentPermission(documentID, deviceID string, authorized bool) (changed bool, err error) {
127		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
128		if err != nil {
129			return false, err
130		}
131		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
132	
133		exists, err := store.DeviceExistsTx(tx, deviceID)
134		if err != nil {
135			return false, err
136		}
137		if !exists {
138			return false, store.ErrDeviceNotFound
139		}
140	
141		current := true // devices start authorized; a row only records a deviation
142		var stored int
143		err = tx.QueryRow(
144			`SELECT authorized FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
145			documentID, deviceID,
146		).Scan(&stored)
147		switch {
148		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
149			// No row: the default (authorized) holds.
150		case err != nil:
151			return false, err
152		default:
153			current = stored != 0
154		}
155		if current == authorized {
156			return false, tx.Commit()
157		}
158	
159		v := 0
160		if authorized {
161			v = 1
162		}
163		if _, err := tx.Exec(
164			`INSERT INTO document_permissions (document_id, device_id, authorized) VALUES (?, ?, ?)
165			 ON CONFLICT (document_id, device_id) DO UPDATE SET authorized = excluded.authorized`,
166			documentID, deviceID, v,
167		); err != nil {
168			return false, err
169		}
170		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
171			return false, err
172		}
173	
174		// A grant cannot unblock a subscription (the first revoke already ended
175		// it, stickily); only a revoke needs to end live subscriptions.
176		if !authorized {
177			s.mu.Lock()
178			sinks := append([]RevokeSink(nil), s.sinks...)
179			s.mu.Unlock()
180			for _, sink := range sinks {
181				sink.PermissionRevoked(documentID, deviceID)
182			}
183		}
184		return true, nil
185	}
186	
187	// DeleteDevicePermissionsTx removes every document-permission ledger row that
188	// names deviceID, inside the caller's transaction: grants and revokes the
189	// deregistered device held on documents vanish together with the device. It is
190	// the permission service's share of device deregistration, run in the same
191	// serialized transaction as the registration layer's cascade, so the row
192	// removals and the device deletion commit as one judgment. After the device
193	// row is gone the default verdict would be "unregistered" anyway; clearing the
194	// rows guarantees a device that later re-registers the same id starts with no
195	// inherited authorization state.
196	func (s *Service) DeleteDevicePermissionsTx(q store.DBTX, deviceID string) error {
197		_, err := q.Exec(
198			`DELETE FROM document_permissions WHERE device_id = ?`, deviceID,
199		)
200		return err
201	}
202	
203	// DocumentAuthorized reports whether deviceID currently holds permission for
204	// documentID. Devices start authorized, so an absent row means authorized.
205	func (s *Service) DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID string) (bool, error) {
206		var stored int
207		err := s.db.QueryRow(
208			`SELECT authorized FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
209			documentID, deviceID,
210		).Scan(&stored)
211		switch {
212		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
213			return true, nil
214		case err != nil:
215			return false, err
216		default:
217			return stored != 0, nil
218		}
219	}
220	
221	// PermissionEntry is one row of a document's permission ledger: a currently
222	// registered device id together with its authorization for the document.
223	type PermissionEntry struct {
224		DeviceID   string
225		Authorized bool
226	}
227	
228	// ListDocumentPermissions is the read-only ledger view of one document: one
229	// entry per currently registered device, in ascending lexicographic device-id
230	// order, paged by limit/offset against that same order.
231	//
232	// A device with no ledger row starts authorized, so its entry reports
233	// Authorized=true; a device whose latest committed action was a revoke reports
234	// false. Deregistered devices carry no device row and their ledger rows were
235	// removed by the deregistration cascade, so they never appear. An unknown
236	// document is indistinguishable from one on which every device keeps the
237	// default: every registered device lists authorized. The read runs in one
238	// serialized transaction, creates no row, moves no cursor and notifies no sink.
239	func (s *Service) ListDocumentPermissions(documentID string, limit, offset int64) ([]PermissionEntry, error) {
240		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
241		if err != nil {
242			return nil, err
243		}
244		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
245	
246		rows, err := tx.Query(
247			`SELECT d.id, COALESCE(p.authorized, 1) AS authorized
248			 FROM devices d
249			 LEFT JOIN document_permissions p
250			   ON p.document_id = ? AND p.device_id = d.id
251			 ORDER BY d.id ASC
252			 LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`,
253			documentID, limit, offset,
254		)
255		if err != nil {
256			return nil, err
257		}
258		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
259	
260		entries := make([]PermissionEntry, 0)
261		for rows.Next() {
262			var entry PermissionEntry
263			var stored int
264			if err := rows.Scan(&entry.DeviceID, &stored); err != nil {
265				return nil, err
266			}
267			entry.Authorized = stored != 0
268			entries = append(entries, entry)
269		}
270		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
271			return nil, err
272		}
273		return entries, tx.Commit()
274	}

14	// changeExportResponse is the export body with the top-level key order fixed
15	// to changes then count. Changes is always a non-nil slice so an empty
16	// export serializes as [] rather than null. Each element is an
17	// events.ListedChange, whose key order is id, deviceId, payload, cursor — the
18	// same record the paged read emits.
19	type changeExportResponse struct {
20		Changes []events.ListedChange `json:"changes"`
21		Count   int                   `json:"count"`
22	}
23	
24	// exportRequested reports whether the query carries the export's from/to
25	// parameters. A present key counts even with an empty value (?from= is the
26	// export with the default bound), matching the document-level collection.
27	func exportRequested(q url.Values) bool {
28		if _, ok := q["from"]; ok {
29			return true
30		}
31		_, ok := q["to"]
32		return ok
33	}
34	
35	// parseExportInterval parses the shared from/to export parameters, writing
36	// the documented 400 on an illegal value. from defaults to 0; a nil to means
37	// the interval has no upper bound; to below from is rejected. It is shared by
38	// the document-scoped and session-scoped exports so their query semantics
39	// cannot drift apart.
40	func parseExportInterval(w http.ResponseWriter, q url.Values) (from int64, to *int64, ok bool) {
41		from = 0
42		if raw := q.Get("from"); raw != "" {
43			v, valid := parseCursorPath(raw)
44			if !valid {
45				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "from must be a non-negative integer")
46				return 0, nil, false
47			}
48			from = v
49		}
50	
51		if raw := q.Get("to"); raw != "" {
52			v, valid := parseCursorPath(raw)
53			if !valid {
54				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "to must be a non-negative integer")
55				return 0, nil, false
56			}
57			to = &v
58		}
59		if to != nil && *to < from {
60			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "to must not be less than from")
61			return 0, nil, false
62		}
63		return from, to, true
64	}
65	
66	// writeChangeExport renders an export result in the shared response shape: a
67	// single compact JSON line with the changes,count key order, an empty export
68	// serializing as [] with count 0.
69	func writeChangeExport(w http.ResponseWriter, rows []events.ListedChange) {
70		if rows == nil {
71			rows = make([]events.ListedChange, 0)
72		}
73		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, changeExportResponse{Changes: rows, Count: len(rows)})
74	}
75	
76	// handleExportChanges is the read-only batch export over a document's change
77	// collection:
78	//
79	//	GET /v1/documents/{documentID}/changes?from=0&to=N
80	//
81	// from defaults to 0; to absent means no upper bound. Only changes whose
82	// cursor is in the closed [from, to] interval and still in the online log are
83	// returned, in ascending cursor order, at most one entry per cursor. An
84	// unknown document or a range without any online change — including one that
85	// lies entirely inside the trimmed region — is a successful 200 with an empty
86	// list and count 0, not an error. Changes compacted out of the online log
87	// never appear. The handler writes nothing: it creates no change, moves no
88	// cursor, records no change and notifies the push channels.
89	func handleExportChanges(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
90		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
91	
92		from, to, ok := parseExportInterval(w, r.URL.Query())
93		if !ok {
94			return
95		}
96	
97		rows, err := s.ExportChanges(documentID, from, to)
98		if err != nil {
99			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to export changes")
100			return
101		}
102		writeChangeExport(w, rows)
103	}
104	
105	// handleSessionExportChanges is the session-scoped view of the change-log
106	// batch export, sharing the session change read's exact collection path:
107	//
108	//	GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes?from=0&to=N
109	//
110	// The interval semantics and the response body are identical to the
111	// document-level export; around them sit the session view's checks in their
112	// fixed order — request shape and parameters (400), session existence (404),
113	// the session device's document permission (403) — so a rejected export
114	// exposes no change content and writes nothing.
115	func handleSessionExportChanges(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
116		sessionID := r.PathValue("sessionId")   // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
117		documentID := r.PathValue("documentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
118	
119		// Malformed interval parameters are a request-shape error (400) checked
120		// before the resource lookup (404), matching the paged read's ordering.
121		from, to, ok := parseExportInterval(w, r.URL.Query())
122		if !ok {
123			return
124		}
125	
126		deviceID, err := s.SessionDevice(sessionID)
127		if err != nil {
128			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSessionNotFound) {
129				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
130				return
131			}
132			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up session")
133			return

136		authorized, err := s.DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID)
137		if err != nil {
138			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up permission")
139			return

154	// malformedChangeExportPath reports whether p targets the change-log
155	// collection's export shape but is not the collection's exact location
156	// (/v1/documents/{documentID}/changes): a trailing slash (an empty trailing
157	// segment) or extra path segments past the collection. The paged read and
158	// this export share that exact collection path; its terminal subresources
159	// (poll, compact, subscribe under the session family) have their own keyword
160	// guards, so only a genuinely unrecognized suffix reaches this check.
161	// ServeMux would answer it with a redirect or a plain-text 404/405; the
162	// change surface promises a JSON error and never a redirect. Empty segments
163	// are already rejected by the guard itself. The keyword is matched only past
164	// the documentID position, so a document literally named "changes" keeps its
165	// ordinary routes.
166	func malformedChangeExportPath(p string) bool {
167		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/documents/")
168		if !ok {
169			return false
170		}
171		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
172		for i, seg := range segs {
173			if seg != "changes" || i == 0 {
174				continue
175			}
176			// Keyword position reached. The collection is exactly
177			// {documentID}/changes; the poll and compact subresources are their own
178			// endpoints and keep their own guards. Anything else (a trailing slash,
179			// an unrecognized extra segment) is a malformed 400.
180			if i == 1 {
181				collection := len(segs) == 2 && segs[0] != ""
182				knownSubresource := len(segs) >= 3 && (segs[2] == "poll" || segs[2] == "compact")
183				return !(collection || knownSubresource)
184			}
185			return false
186		}
187		return false
188	}

190	// malformedSessionChangesPath reports whether p targets the session-scoped
191	// change collection's shape but is not the collection's exact location
192	// (/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes): extra path
193	// segments past the collection. The paged read and the interval export share
194	// that exact collection path; the subscribe subresource has its own endpoint
195	// and keyword guard, so only a genuinely unrecognized suffix reaches this
196	// check. ServeMux would answer it with a plain-text 404; the change surface
197	// promises a JSON 400 and never a redirect. Empty segments (doubled slashes,
198	// a trailing slash) are already rejected by the guard itself.
199	//
200	// "changes" is treated as the collection keyword only in the fourth segment,
201	// right after the document identifier; a session or document identifier
202	// literally named "changes" occupies an identifier position and keeps its
203	// ordinary routes.
204	func malformedSessionChangesPath(p string) bool {
205		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
206		if !ok {
207			return false
208		}
209		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
210		// The CRDT namespace ("crdt" immediately past the document identifier)
211		// has its own guard; "changes" there is an ordinary identifier, not this
212		// collection's keyword.
213		if len(segs) >= 4 && segs[1] == "documents" && segs[3] == "crdt" {
214			return false
215		}
216		if len(segs) < 4 || segs[1] != "documents" || segs[3] != "changes" {
217			return false
218		}
219		// Keyword position reached. The collection is exactly
220		// {sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes; the subscribe subresource
221		// adds one trailing "subscribe" segment and keeps its own guard; the long
222		// poll adds one trailing "poll" segment and keeps its own guard; the
223		// offline replay adds one trailing "replay" segment and keeps its own
224		// guard. Anything else past the keyword is a malformed 400.
225		collection := len(segs) == 4 && segs[0] != "" && segs[2] != ""
226		subscribe := len(segs) == 5 && segs[4] == "subscribe"
227		poll := len(segs) == 5 && segs[4] == "poll"
228		replay := len(segs) == 5 && segs[4] == "replay"
229		return !(collection || subscribe || poll || replay)
230	}

232	// malformedSessionPollPath reports whether p targets the session-scoped
233	// long-poll endpoint but is not at its exact location
234	// (/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes/poll): a missing
235	// "documents"/"changes" segment, an extra segment, or a "poll" segment in a
236	// position short of the registered shape. ServeMux would answer those with a
237	// plain-text 404 (or a redirect for an empty segment); every failure of this
238	// endpoint must be a JSON 400 instead. Empty segments are already rejected by
239	// the guard itself.
240	//
241	// "poll" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in its terminal segment
242	// position (the fifth segment, index 4); a session or document identifier
243	// literally named "poll" occupies an identifier position (index 0 or 2) and is
244	// therefore left to the ordinary changes routes like any other id.
245	func malformedSessionPollPath(p string) bool {
246		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
247		if !ok {
248			return false
249		}
250		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
251		// The CRDT namespace ("crdt" immediately past the document identifier)
252		// has its own guard; "poll" there is an ordinary identifier, not the

254		if len(segs) >= 4 && segs[1] == "documents" && segs[3] == "crdt" {
255			return false
256		}
257		for i, seg := range segs {

259				continue
260			}

262			// "poll" there is an ordinary identifier, not the endpoint word.
263			if i == 0 || i == 2 {

265			}

267			// with the documents/changes scaffolding around it, and no segment may
268			// follow. Any other occurrence is a malformed path.
269			if i == 4 && len(segs) == 5 &&
270				segs[0] != "" &&
271				segs[1] == "documents" &&
272				segs[2] != "" &&
273				segs[3] == "changes" {
274				return false
275			}
276			return true
277		}
278		return false
279	}

282	// offline replay endpoint but is not at its exact location
283	// (/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes/replay): a missing
284	// "documents"/"changes" segment, an extra segment, or a "replay" segment in a
285	// position short of the registered shape. ServeMux would answer those with a
286	// plain-text 404 (or a redirect for an empty segment); every failure of this
287	// endpoint must be a JSON 400 instead. Empty segments are already rejected by
288	// the guard itself.
289	//
290	// "replay" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in its terminal segment
291	// position (the fifth segment, index 4); a session or document identifier
292	// literally named "replay" occupies an identifier position (index 0 or 2) and
293	// is therefore left to the ordinary changes routes like any other id.
294	func malformedSessionReplayPath(p string) bool {
295		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
296		if !ok {
297			return false
298		}
299		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
300		// The CRDT namespace ("crdt" immediately past the document identifier)
301		// has its own guard; "replay" there is an ordinary identifier, not the
302		// changes-replay keyword.
303		if len(segs) >= 4 && segs[1] == "documents" && segs[3] == "crdt" {
304			return false
305		}
306		for i, seg := range segs {
307			if seg != "replay" {
308				continue
309			}
310			// Identifier positions: sessionId (0) and documentId (2). A value of
311			// "replay" there is an ordinary identifier, not the endpoint word.
312			if i == 0 || i == 2 {
313				continue
314			}
315			// Endpoint keyword position: the fifth segment must be exactly
316			// "replay" with the documents/changes scaffolding around it, and no
317			// segment may follow. Any other occurrence is a malformed path.
318			if i == 4 && len(segs) == 5 &&
319				segs[0] != "" &&
320				segs[1] == "documents" &&
321				segs[2] != "" &&
322				segs[3] == "changes" {
323				return false
324			}
325			return true
326		}
327		return false
328	}

1	package server
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"errors"
6		"net/http"
7		"strings"
8	
9		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/app"
10		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/events"
11		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
12	)
13	
14	// snapshotExportItem is one element of an export body. The struct field order
15	// fixes the on-the-wire key order to cursor then state; State is embedded as
16	// raw JSON so the stored content is emitted verbatim, exactly as the single
17	// snapshot read emits it.
18	type snapshotExportItem struct {
19		Cursor int64           `json:"cursor"`
20		State  json.RawMessage `json:"state"`
21	}
22	
23	// snapshotExportResponse is the export body with the top-level key order fixed
24	// to snapshots then count. Snapshots is always a non-nil slice so an empty
25	// export serializes as [] rather than null.
26	type snapshotExportResponse struct {
27		Snapshots []snapshotExportItem `json:"snapshots"`
28		Count     int                  `json:"count"`
29	}
30	
31	// handleExportSnapshots is the read-only batch export over a document's
32	// snapshot collection:
33	//
34	//	GET /v1/documents/{documentID}/snapshots?from=0&to=N
35	//
36	// from defaults to 0; to absent means no upper bound. Only snapshots whose
37	// cursor is in the closed [from, to] interval are returned, in ascending
38	// cursor order, at most one entry per cursor. An unknown document or a range
39	// without any snapshot is a successful 200 with an empty list and count 0, not
40	// an error. The handler writes nothing: it creates no snapshot, moves no
41	// cursor, records no change and notifies the push channels.
42	func handleExportSnapshots(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
43		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
44	
45		from, to, ok := parseExportInterval(w, r.URL.Query())
46		if !ok {
47			return
48		}
49	
50		snaps, err := s.ExportSnapshots(documentID, from, to)
51		if err != nil {
52			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to export snapshots")
53			return
54		}
55		writeSnapshotExport(w, snaps)
56	}
57	
58	// writeSnapshotExport renders an export result in the shared response shape: a
59	// single compact JSON line with the snapshots,count key order, each item
60	// keyed cursor,state, an empty export serializing as [] with count 0. It is
61	// shared by the document-scoped and session-scoped exports so their bodies
62	// cannot drift apart.
63	func writeSnapshotExport(w http.ResponseWriter, snaps []events.ExportedSnapshot) {
64		items := make([]snapshotExportItem, 0, len(snaps))
65		for _, snap := range snaps {
66			items = append(items, snapshotExportItem{Cursor: snap.Cursor, State: snap.State})
67		}
68		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, snapshotExportResponse{Snapshots: items, Count: len(items)})
69	}
70	
71	// handleSessionExportSnapshots is the session-scoped view of the snapshot
72	// batch export, over the session document-read prefix with the resource
73	// segment swapped to the snapshot collection:
74	//
75	//	GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/snapshots?from=0&to=N
76	//
77	// The interval semantics and the response body are identical to the
78	// document-level export; the path offers no other read form, so every GET is
79	// the export (from/to absent means the default interval). Around the export
80	// sit the session view's checks in their fixed order — request shape and
81	// parameters (400), session existence (404), the session device's document
82	// permission (403) — so a rejected export exposes no snapshot content and
83	// writes nothing.
84	func handleSessionExportSnapshots(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
85		sessionID := r.PathValue("sessionId")   // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
86		documentID := r.PathValue("documentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
87	
88		// Malformed interval parameters are a request-shape error (400) checked
89		// before the resource lookup (404), matching the session change export's
90		// ordering.
91		from, to, ok := parseExportInterval(w, r.URL.Query())
92		if !ok {
93			return
94		}
95	
96		deviceID, err := s.SessionDevice(sessionID)
97		if err != nil {
98			if errors.Is(err, store.ErrSessionNotFound) {
99				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "session not found")
100				return
101			}
102			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up session")
103			return
104		}
105	
106		authorized, err := s.DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID)
107		if err != nil {
108			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to look up permission")
109			return
110		}
111		if !authorized {
112			writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
113			return
114		}
115	
116		snaps, err := s.ExportSnapshots(documentID, from, to)
117		if err != nil {
118			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to export snapshots")
119			return
120		}
121		writeSnapshotExport(w, snaps)
122	}
123	
124	// malformedSnapshotPath reports whether p targets the snapshot namespace but
125	// is not at one of its two exact locations:
126	//
127	//	GET  /v1/documents/{documentID}/snapshots          (the batch export)
128	//	GET  /v1/documents/{documentID}/snapshots/{cursor} (the single read)
129	//
130	// A trailing slash (an empty cursor segment, including the collection path
131	// with a trailing slash), extra path segments, or a "snapshots" segment in any
132	// keyword position short of one of those shapes is a malformed 400 rather than
133	// ServeMux's redirect or plain-text 404/405: the snapshot endpoints promise a
134	// JSON error and never a redirect. Empty segments are already rejected by the
135	// guard itself. The keyword is matched only past the documentID position, so a
136	// document literally named "snapshots" keeps its ordinary routes.
137	func malformedSnapshotPath(p string) bool {
138		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/documents/")
139		if !ok {
140			return false
141		}
142		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
143		for i, seg := range segs {
144			if seg != "snapshots" || i == 0 {
145				continue
146			}
147			// Keyword position reached. The collection is exactly
148			// {documentID}/snapshots; the single read adds one non-empty cursor
149			// segment. Anything else (trailing slash, missing/extra segments) is
150			// malformed.
151			collection := len(segs) == 2 && segs[0] != ""
152			item := len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[2] != ""
153			return !(collection || item)
154		}
155		return false
156	}
157	
158	// malformedSessionSnapshotsPath reports whether p targets the session-scoped
159	// snapshot collection's shape but is not the collection's exact location
160	// (/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/snapshots): extra path
161	// segments past the collection (the session view has no single-snapshot
162	// item, so a trailing cursor segment is malformed too). ServeMux would answer
163	// those with a plain-text 404; the snapshot surface promises a JSON 400 and
164	// never a redirect. Empty segments (doubled slashes, a trailing slash) are
165	// already rejected by the guard itself.
166	//
167	// "snapshots" is treated as the collection keyword only in the fourth
168	// segment, right after the document identifier; a session or document
169	// identifier literally named "snapshots" occupies an identifier position and
170	// keeps its ordinary routes.
171	func malformedSessionSnapshotsPath(p string) bool {
172		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
173		if !ok {
174			return false
175		}
176		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
177		// The CRDT namespace ("crdt" immediately past the document identifier)
178		// has its own guard; "snapshots" there is an ordinary identifier, not
179		// this collection's keyword.
180		if len(segs) >= 4 && segs[1] == "documents" && segs[3] == "crdt" {
181			return false
182		}
183		if len(segs) < 4 || segs[1] != "documents" || segs[3] != "snapshots" {
184			return false
185		}
186		// Keyword position reached. The collection is exactly
187		// {sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/snapshots; anything past it is a
188		// malformed 400.
189		return !(len(segs) == 4 && segs[0] != "" && segs[2] != "")
190	}
